answer: To suppress Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor node identities to open-path optical dispersion. A node verifies presence by aiming dual-wavelength pulses across a river at a corner-cube prism on a surveyed knoll, measuring chromatic transit delays. An attacker must operate discrete, precision beam-steering optics and occupy separate physical sightlines per identity, incurring heavy hardware and siting costs. However, dense evaporative fog frequently degrades beam coherence.
